Energy consumption and effort: airports and football¶

Energy and effort of the experiments run so far, in five parts:

  1. Airports, Strategy A (LLM alone, 9 prompts of Figure 2), with and without context.
  2. Airports, Strategy B (agent with web search; search only, and search + memory), context on.
  3. Airports, Strategy A vs Strategy B.
  4. Football, Strategy A, with and without context (Strategy B on football is still running and is not included).
  5. Both datasets, Strategy A.

Data. Every ok run of the 5 models (gpt-oss:20b, gemma4:31b, gpt-oss:120b, mistral-large-3, deepseek-v4.1-flash), 3 runs per task:

Dataset Set Tasks Strategy
airports v5 context on 243 A (9 prompts), B search, B search + memory
airports v5 context off 180 (tasks that have a context-free version) A (9 prompts)
football v1 idmix context on 239 A (9 prompts)
football v1 idmix context off 233 A (9 prompts)

Energy (as in v5_eis.ipynb and the paper draft):

  • LLM energy (EC): the EcoLogits estimate of each LLM call, summed over the run's calls (repair calls included), with its global warming potential (GWP, g CO₂e) and water consumption footprint (WCF, mL). deepseek-v4.1-flash has no EcoLogits entry; its estimate uses a stand-in of similar total size.
  • Run energy E_run = N_calls · E_single + N_searches · e_search, with e_search = 0.3 Wh per web search (Google, 2009; §3.4 varies it). Strategy A makes no search, so its run energy is its LLM energy. Searches are counted whether or not our search cache answered them (a user without the cache would make them). GWP and WCF of a search are those of the run's own LLM calls per Wh.
  • All values are estimates, not measurements at Ollama.

Effort (METRICS.md §6), from the effort block of every run:

  • PFE: tokens of the template (instructions and examples, without placeholders). Strategy B: the plan and synthesis templates together.
  • $T_{user}$ (human tokens): the tokens a person writes for one task = template + known properties (input) + context + target names.
  • KLM: time to type and send the prompt (keystroke-level model): M + N_chars·K + H + P + K, with K = 0.28 s, M = 1.35 s, H = 0.4 s, P = 1.1 s, assuming the whole prompt is typed.
  • $T_{process}$: the tokens the model processes in a run: input and output, reasoning included, over all LLM calls.
  • Token amplification $= |T_{process}| \,/\, |T_{user}|$: how much work the system does for each token of human effort. For Strategy B it includes the retrieved evidence the synthesis call reads.
  • Output ratio $= |T_{out}| \,/\, |T_{user}|$ (output tokens, reasoning included): a secondary measure, the part of $T_{process}$ the model generates.

Every F1 is also given with abstentions ignored, F1 (ign.) = 2c / (2c + w), next to F1 = 2c / (2c + 2w + a).

PLAIN = FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:g}")   # log axes labelled 0.1, 2, 5 rather than 10⁻¹, 2×10⁰
MINOR25 = FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:g}" if f"{v:g}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")[-1:] in ("2", "5") else "")


def logaxis(ax, which="y", minor=False):
    # log scale with plain labels (0.001, 0.01, 1, 2, 5), minor labels at 2 and 5 when the range is short
    for a in which:
        axis = ax.xaxis if a == "x" else ax.yaxis
        (ax.set_xscale if a == "x" else ax.set_yscale)("log")
        axis.set_major_formatter(PLAIN)
        axis.set_minor_formatter(MINOR25 if minor else FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: ""))


def fig1(w=9, h=5):
    # every saved figure is a single chart with its own title, axis labels and legend
    return plt.subplots(figsize=(w, h))


def save(fig, name):
    fig.tight_layout()
    for ext in ("png", "pdf"):
        fig.savefig(FIG / f"{name}.{ext}", bbox_inches="tight", dpi=200)
    plt.show()


def model_handles():
    return [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="", marker="o", color=MCOLOR[m], ms=7, label=MNAME[m]) for m in MODELS]


def heading(text):
    return plt.Line2D([], [], ls="", marker="", label=text)


def legend(ax, groups, **kw):
    # one legend with a heading per group, e.g. [("model", handles), ("approach", handles)]
    h = []
    for i, (title, hs) in enumerate(groups):
        h += ([heading("")] if i else []) + [heading(title)] + list(hs)
    lg = ax.legend(handles=h, fontsize=8, handletextpad=0.4, **kw)
    for t, hh in zip(lg.get_texts(), h):
        if hh.get_marker() in ("", "None", None) and t.get_text():
            t.set_fontweight("bold"); t.set_position((-14, 0))
    return lg


def model_legend(ax, **kw):
    return legend(ax, [("model", model_handles())], **kw)

runs["human_tokens"] = runs[[f"{p}_tokens" for p in ("template", "input", "context", "targets")]].sum(axis=1)
runs["human_chars"] = runs[[f"{p}_chars" for p in ("template", "input", "context", "targets")]].sum(axis=1)
runs["klm_s"] = M_ + runs.human_chars * K + H + P + K
runs["amp_out"] = runs.tokens_out / runs.human_tokens
runs["amp_proc"] = (runs.tokens_in + runs.tokens_out) / runs.human_tokens
runs["EC_search"] = runs.searches * E_SEARCH_WH
runs["EC_run"] = runs.EC_wh + runs.EC_search
scale = np.where(runs.EC_wh > 0, runs.EC_run / runs.EC_wh, 1.0)   # GWP and WCF of a search: those of the run's LLM calls per Wh
runs["GWP_run"], runs["WCF_run"] = runs.GWP_g * scale, runs.WCF_ml * scale
# check the run energy against the evaluation's formula (METRICS.md §4.2) on a sample
s = runs[runs.searches > 0].head(200)
chk = [1000 * agent_energy(e / 1000, n, t, E_SEARCH_WH / (e / n)) for e, n, t in zip(s.EC_wh, s.llm_calls, s.searches)]
assert np.allclose(chk, s.EC_run), "run energy differs from evaluation.eis.agent_energy"

def configs(dataset, set_, strategy):
    # one row per model × variant: means per run, accuracy and energy per correct answer
    r = runs[(runs.dataset == dataset) & (runs.set == set_) & runs.strategy.isin(strategy if isinstance(strategy, list) else [strategy])]
    c = (r.groupby(["model", "variant"])
          .agg(runs=("task_id", "size"), tasks=("task_id", "nunique"), llm_calls=("llm_calls", "mean"), searches=("searches", "mean"),
               searches_real=("searches_real", "mean"), tokens_in=("tokens_in", "mean"), tokens_out=("tokens_out", "mean"),
               tokens_reasoning=("tokens_reasoning", "mean"), evidence_tokens=("evidence_tokens", "mean"),
               EC_llm=("EC_wh", "mean"), EC_search=("EC_search", "mean"), EC_run=("EC_run", "mean"),
               GWP=("GWP_run", "mean"), WCF=("WCF_run", "mean"), EC_total=("EC_run", "sum"), EC_llm_total=("EC_wh", "sum"),
               PFE=("template_tokens", "mean"), human_tokens=("human_tokens", "mean"), klm_s=("klm_s", "mean"),
               amp_out=("amp_out", "mean"), amp_proc=("amp_proc", "mean"), latency_s=("latency_s", "median"),
               cost_usd=("cost_usd", "sum"))
          .reset_index())
    a = acc[(acc.dataset == dataset) & (acc.set == set_)]
    c = c.merge(a[["model", "variant", "correct", "wrong", "abstained", "f1", "f1_ign", "abstention"]], on=["model", "variant"], how="left")
    c["Wh_per_correct"] = c.EC_total / c.correct.replace(0, np.nan)
    c["Wh_per_correct_llm"] = c.EC_llm_total / c.correct.replace(0, np.nan)
    c["search_share"] = c.EC_search / c.EC_run
    return c

def best_prompt(c):
    # each model's Strategy A prompt with the highest F1 (as in the other reports)
    a = c[c.variant.isin(PROMPTS)]
    return a.loc[a.groupby("model").f1.idxmax()].set_index("model").variant.to_dict()

def order(df, col="model"):
    return df.assign(_o=df[col].map({m: i for i, m in enumerate(MODELS)})).sort_values(["_o"] + ([ "variant"] if "variant" in df else [])).drop(columns="_o")

FMT = {"llm_calls": "{:.2f}", "searches": "{:.2f}", "searches_real": "{:.2f}", "tokens_in": "{:.0f}", "tokens_out": "{:.0f}",
       "tokens_reasoning": "{:.0f}", "evidence_tokens": "{:.0f}", "EC_llm": "{:.4f}", "EC_search": "{:.3f}", "EC_run": "{:.4f}",
       "GWP": "{:.4f}", "WCF": "{:.3f}", "PFE": "{:.0f}", "human_tokens": "{:.0f}", "klm_s": "{:.0f}", "amp_out": "{:.2f}",
       "amp_proc": "{:.2f}", "Wh_per_correct": "{:.3f}", "Wh_per_correct_llm": "{:.3f}", "search_share": "{:.0%}",
       "f1": "{:.3f}", "f1_ign": "{:.3f}", "abstention": "{:.0%}", "latency_s": "{:.1f}", "cost_usd": "${:.2f}"}
COLS = {"llm_calls": "LLM calls", "searches": "searches", "searches_real": "searches (not cached)", "tokens_in": "tokens in",
        "tokens_out": "tokens out", "tokens_reasoning": "of which reasoning", "evidence_tokens": "evidence tokens",
        "EC_llm": "EC LLM (Wh)", "EC_search": "EC searches (Wh)", "EC_run": "E_run (Wh)", "GWP": "GWP (g CO₂e)",
        "WCF": "WCF (mL)", "PFE": "PFE", "human_tokens": "|T_user| (human tokens)", "klm_s": "KLM (s)", "amp_out": "output ratio |T_out|/|T_user|",
        "amp_proc": "token ampl. |T_process|/|T_user|", "Wh_per_correct": "Wh per correct", "Wh_per_correct_llm": "Wh per correct (LLM only)",
        "search_share": "searches' share of E_run", "f1": "F1", "f1_ign": "F1 (ign.)", "abstention": "abstention",
        "latency_s": "median latency (s)", "cost_usd": "cost (USD)"}

def show(df, cols, index=("model",), caption=None):
    d = df.copy()
    if "model" in d:
        d["model"] = d.model.map(MNAME)
    if "variant" in d:
        d["variant"] = d.variant.map(lambda v: PNAME.get(v, v))
    d = d[list(index) + cols].rename(columns=COLS)
    st = d.style.hide(axis="index").format({COLS[k]: v for k, v in FMT.items() if k in cols})
    if caption:
        st = st.set_caption(caption)
    display(st)

C = {(d, s, "A"): configs(d, s, "A") for d in ("airports", "football") for s in ("ctx", "noctx")}
C[("airports", "ctx", "B")] = configs("airports", "ctx", ["B", "B_memory"])   # both B variants

1.3 Context on vs off¶

The context-off set has its own tasks (for airports, the 180 tasks that have a context-free version), so these are means over each set, not paired tasks.

What Strategy A on airports shows.

  • The model sets the energy, not the prompt. Mean energy per run (context on) spans two orders of magnitude:

    • gemma4:31b 0.0010 Wh;
    • gpt-oss:20b 0.0085 Wh;
    • gpt-oss:120b 0.023 Wh;
    • deepseek-v4.1-flash 0.040 Wh (stand-in estimate);
    • mistral-large-3 0.096 Wh.

    Within a model, the 9 prompts change it by a factor of 1.5 (deepseek) to 4.4 (gemma4).

  • Which prompt costs most depends on the model.

    • The compact prompt is the most expensive for four models (gemma4 0.0030 Wh against 0.0007 for the others), because without the output only the header row instruction the models write more.
    • For mistral-large-3 the CoT prompts cost most (0.128–0.132 Wh against 0.049 for zero-shot).

  • Strategy A does little work per human token. Token amplification $|T_{process}|/|T_{user}|$ is 1.2–3.9: the model processes the person's prompt, its fixed wrapping (chat format, labels) and a short answer.

    • Mean over the 9 prompts: deepseek 1.31, mistral-large-3 1.39, gemma4 1.43, gpt-oss:120b 1.88, gpt-oss:20b 2.09. The gpt-oss models are highest because they generate 106–155 tokens per run, 88–92% of them hidden reasoning; the other three generate 11–29.
    • Amplification falls as the template grows (gpt-oss:20b from 2.13 at zero-shot to 1.62 at 5-shot) and is highest for compact (1.72–3.92), the shortest prompt: the work stays about the same while the person writes more.
    • The model's own output is below the person's text: the output ratio $|T_{out}|/|T_{user}|$ is under 1 except for compact with the two gpt-oss models (1.78 and 1.24).

  • More prompt effort does not buy accuracy.

    • PFE goes from 81 (compact) to 427 tokens (5-shot + CoT), and KLM from about 3 to 9 minutes, while the mean F1 over models stays at 0.173–0.183.
    • F1 (ign.) is lowest for compact (0.33) and 0.39–0.43 for the others.

  • Energy per correct answer ranges from 0.024 Wh (gemma4) to 1.6 Wh (mistral-large-3), a factor of 65.

  • GWP does not follow energy across models. EcoLogits gives mistral-large-3 and deepseek a lower-carbon electricity mix: mistral emits 0.009 g CO₂e per run at 0.096 Wh, about the same as gpt-oss:120b at 0.023 Wh. WCF follows energy.

  • Context costs almost nothing. It adds about 21 tokens to $|T_{user}|$ and 20–25 input tokens per task; token amplification is 0.95–1.0 times the value without context. Energy with context is 0.83–1.16 times the energy without (the two sets have different tasks, so this is not a paired comparison).

2. Airports, Strategy B¶

Context on, 243 tasks, 3 runs each. Search + memory replays the plan and searches of search (no new search) and lets the synthesis call use the model's own knowledge; its searches are those of the replayed run, counted again, since a user without our cache would make them.

Other model input is what the two calls read beyond the person's text and the evidence: the plan's output passed to the synthesis call, the search results' titles and URLs, and the template counted twice (plan and synthesis each include their template). It is clipped at 0 where the effort count is larger.

What Strategy B on airports shows.

  • The agent reads about 10 times more than Strategy A. Each run makes 2 LLM calls (plan and synthesis) and 1.2 (gemma4) to 3.0 (mistral) searches. The two calls read 3,200–3,900 input tokens, of which 2,100–2,750 are retrieved evidence.
  • The LLM calls alone use 0.0075 (gemma4) to 0.77 Wh (mistral-large-3) per run.
  • With searches at 0.3 Wh each, a run uses 0.36–1.67 Wh.
    • Searches make up 91–98% of that for gemma4 and the two gpt-oss models, and 54–68% for mistral-large-3 and deepseek.
    • A search costs the same whichever model asks for it, so it weighs most on small models.
  • Memory adds no search and almost no energy (≤ 0.08 Wh more LLM energy per run). It lowers the energy per correct answer where it raises accuracy: gemma4 from 10.1 to 6.9 Wh, deepseek from 34.4 to 21.6 Wh.
  • The person's effort is larger but is written once.
    • The plan and synthesis templates are 525 tokens (537 with memory), against 81–427 for Strategy A, and KLM rises to about 12 minutes.
    • Per task, the person writes only the known values and target names, as in Strategy A.
  • Token amplification $|T_{process}|/|T_{user}|$ is 5.7–7.2 (5.6–7.2 with memory), against 1.2–3.9 for Strategy A: for every token the person writes, the two calls process 6–7, mostly evidence the person did not write.
  • The output ratio $|T_{out}|/|T_{user}|$ stays below 1 (0.17–0.71): the agent's extra work is reading, not writing.
  • Energy per correct answer is 6.9–34 Wh with searches, and 0.15–11 Wh for the LLM calls alone.

3. Airports, Strategy A vs Strategy B¶

Context on, the same 243 tasks. For each model: Strategy A's zero-shot prompt and its best prompt (highest F1), and Strategy B's two variants.

APPS = ["A: zero-shot", "A: best", "B: search", "B: search + memory"]

ab["app"] = ab.approach.str.replace(r" \(.*\)", "", regex=True)
def approach_legend(ax, extra=(), models=True, **kw):
    # colour = model (left out where the axis already names the models), marker = approach
    h = [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="", marker=AMARK[a], color=INK2, ms=7, label=a) for a in APPS] + list(extra)
    legend(ax, ([("model", model_handles())] if models else []) + [("approach", h)], **kw)

            r = ab[(ab.model == m) & (ab.app == a)].iloc[0]
            ax.scatter(r.EC_run, r[col], marker=AMARK[a], s=70, color=MCOLOR[m], edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.5, zorder=3)
    logaxis(ax, "x"); ax.set_xlabel("Wh per run (log)"); ax.set_ylabel(f"{lab}, voted over 3 runs")
    small = plt.Line2D([], [], ls="", marker="o", color=INK2, alpha=0.4, ms=4, label="A: other prompts")
    approach_legend(ax, [small], loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1))
    ax.set_title(f"Airports, context on: {lab} vs energy per run, A vs B", fontsize=11)
    save(fig, f"airports_AB_{fn}_vs_energy")

3.1 Sensitivity to the energy of a search¶

The energy of a web search is not reported by the provider; the ratio B ÷ A best per run as a function of it (0 = LLM calls only).

In [12]:
es = np.logspace(-3, 0, 60)
fig, ax = fig1(9, 5)
for m in MODELS:
    ax.plot(es, (bs.loc[m].EC_llm + bs.loc[m].searches * es) / best.loc[m].EC_run, color=MCOLOR[m], lw=2, label=MNAME[m])
ax.axvline(E_SEARCH_WH, color=INK2, ls="--", lw=1, label=f"value used in this report ({E_SEARCH_WH} Wh)")
logaxis(ax, "xy")
ax.set_xlabel("energy of one web search (Wh, log)"); ax.set_ylabel("E_run of B (search) ÷ E_run of A best prompt (log)")
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
ax.set_title("Airports, context on: B ÷ A energy per run vs the energy of a search")
save(fig, "airports_AB_search_sensitivity")

What the comparison shows (airports, context on).

  • The agent uses 13 to 521 times the energy per run of the same model's best Strategy A prompt. By model:
    • mistral-large-3 12.7×;
    • deepseek 27×;
    • gpt-oss:120b 29×;
    • gpt-oss:20b 75×;
    • gemma4 521×.
  • Without the searches the factor is 2.3–11. The rest is the searches.
  • The LLM part grows for two reasons.
    • There are two calls instead of one.
    • The synthesis call reads the evidence: 5–10 times more tokens processed, and 2.3–15 times more tokens generated.
  • The person writes 1.2–4.4 times more tokens. This is the B templates against the best A prompt; for gpt-oss:120b the best A prompt is compact, the shortest.
  • Per correct answer the agent costs 10–660 times more (11–450 times with memory).
  • Accuracy gains do not offset the cost.
    • B search is ahead in F1 for gpt-oss:20b (+0.088), gpt-oss:120b (+0.080) and mistral-large-3 (+0.074), and behind for gemma4 (−0.031) and deepseek (−0.068).
    • With abstentions ignored it is ahead for four models (+0.04 to +0.22) and level for gemma4 (−0.010).
  • Where the trade-off sits. Each model's highest-F1 configuration is its agent, at its highest energy. The lowest-energy configuration overall, gemma4 with Strategy A, reaches F1 0.19 / 0.48: above gpt-oss:20b with any Strategy A prompt, and at 1/500 of the agent's energy.
  • The size of the factor depends on the unmeasured energy of a search; its sign does not. With no search energy, B uses 2.3–11 times A's energy; at 1 Wh per search, 29–1,710 times (v5_eis.ipynb §5).

4.3 Context on vs off¶

The context-off set has its own tasks (for airports, the 180 tasks that have a context-free version), so these are means over each set, not paired tasks.

What Strategy A on football shows.

  • The same ordering of models as on airports. Energy per run (context on):
    • gemma4:31b 0.0008 Wh;
    • gpt-oss:20b 0.0065 Wh;
    • gpt-oss:120b 0.018 Wh;
    • deepseek 0.040 Wh;
    • mistral-large-3 0.077 Wh.
  • The prompts behave as on airports.
    • Compact is the most expensive prompt for all five models, and has the highest token amplification $|T_{process}|/|T_{user}|$ (1.42–3.94).
    • Token amplification falls as the template grows (1.10–1.43 at 5-shot); mean over the prompts 1.17 (deepseek) to 1.87 (gpt-oss:20b).
  • Prompt effort and accuracy are not aligned here either.
    • Compact, the cheapest prompt to write (PFE 81, KLM about 2.7 min), has the highest mean F1 (0.273), because it makes the models abstain less.
    • The examples raise F1 (ign.): 0.68–0.70 with 3 or 5 shots against 0.55 at zero-shot, at 3–4 times the PFE.
  • Energy per correct answer ranges from 0.030 Wh (gemma4) to 1.13 Wh (gpt-oss:120b). gpt-oss:120b is the most expensive per correct answer because it abstains most; per run it is mid-range.
  • Context changes nothing measurable. It adds about 2 tokens to $|T_{user}|$ per task on average (it only changes 33 high-stratum tasks), and the energy with and without context differs by at most 3% per model.

5. Both datasets, Strategy A¶

Strategy A on airports (v5) and football (v1 idmix), context on unless said otherwise. The prompts and models are the same, and both task sets give 1–5 known properties (3 on average) and ask for one. They differ in where those properties sit: on airports most are context (neighbouring nodes, ~37 tokens per task), on football most are the player's own properties (~29 tokens) with little context (~4 tokens).

    ax.set_title(f"Strategy A, context on: {lab} vs energy, both datasets\none point per model × prompt", fontsize=11)
    save(fig, f"both_A_{fn}_vs_energy")

What the two datasets together show (Strategy A).

  • Energy per run is a property of the model. The two datasets differ by at most 25% per model, against a factor of about 100 between models.
    • Football runs are slightly cheaper: shorter prompts (338–402 input tokens against 404–465) and, for the gpt-oss models, shorter reasoning (113 against 155 output tokens for gpt-oss:20b).
  • Token amplification $|T_{process}|/|T_{user}|$ is also set by the model. Mean over the prompts, the gpt-oss models are at 1.7–2.1 on both datasets, because 85–92% of their output is reasoning; gemma4, mistral and deepseek are at 1.2–1.4. It is 0.14–0.22 lower on football, where the model receives fewer tokens beyond what the person writes.
  • Energy per correct answer depends on accuracy, so it differs by dataset.
    • Lower on football for mistral-large-3 (0.84 against 1.60 Wh), deepseek (0.37 against 0.70) and gpt-oss:20b (0.20 against 0.23).
    • Higher for gpt-oss:120b (1.13 against 0.51) and gemma4 (0.030 against 0.024).
  • Totals.
    • Context on, all 45 model × prompt configurations used 1,107 Wh on airports (32,804 runs) and 918 Wh on football (32,261 runs). That is 0.71 and 0.50 Wh per correct voted answer.
    • Without context: 764 Wh and 910 Wh (0.42 and 0.52 Wh per correct answer).
    • At list prices the runs cost $3.06–4.34 per set.
  • Football's higher F1 is not a gain in efficiency. Many football statistics have an easy most-frequent value (a constant guess scores F1 0.393 / 0.565 there), so the lower energy per correct answer comes partly from guessable answers.
  • More energy does not mean higher F1. Across the 90 Strategy A configurations of the two datasets there is no upward trend: the highest F1 (ign.) values on football are reached by gpt-oss:120b (0.80 at 0.016 Wh per run), gpt-oss:20b (0.77 at 0.006 Wh) and gemma4 (0.74 at 0.0006 Wh), not by the two most energy-hungry models.

6. Summary¶

  1. The model decides the energy. With Strategy A, energy per run ranges from 0.0008 Wh (gemma4:31b) to 0.1 Wh (mistral-large-3) on both datasets. Prompts change it by a factor of 1.5–6 (most for gemma4), the dataset by at most 25%, and context by under 16% (under 3% on football).
  2. The agent adds one to two orders of magnitude. On airports, Strategy B uses 0.36–1.67 Wh per run, 13–521 times its model's best Strategy A prompt. 54–98% of that is the web searches (at 0.3 Wh each); the LLM calls alone are 2.3–11 times A. Memory adds almost nothing.
  3. The agent multiplies the work per human token. Token amplification $|T_{process}|/|T_{user}|$ is 1.1–3.9 for Strategy A (highest for the compact prompt and the gpt-oss models, 85–92% of whose output is hidden reasoning) and 5.6–7.2 for the agent, mostly retrieved evidence. The models' own output stays below the person's text almost everywhere (output ratio < 1).
  4. Effort and accuracy are weakly linked. Longer prompts (PFE 81 → 427, KLM about 3 → 9 min) do not raise F1 on airports. On football they raise F1 (ign.) but lower F1 compared with the compact prompt. The agent's templates (525 tokens) are written once.
  5. Per correct answer, Strategy A needs 0.02–1.6 Wh and the agent 7–34 Wh. The agent's accuracy gain (up to +0.09 F1, +0.22 F1 (ign.)) costs 10–660 times more energy per correct answer.

Caveats.

  • All energies are EcoLogits estimates; deepseek's uses a stand-in model.
  • The energy of a search (0.3 Wh) is a 2009 figure for another service. The conclusions about the agent hold for any value from 0 to 1 Wh, but the factors do not.
  • Football Strategy B is still running and will be added when complete.
